newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New Manila bourse chief wants more local investors.
newsitem.headline: New Manila bourse chief wants more local investors.

text.p: Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) president Jose Luis Yulo said on Friday his main agenda was to attract more domestic investors into the equities market and make stocks trading a national sport.
It is estimated that only one percent of Filipinos own shares of publicly listed companies. At present, there are 221 listed companies listed in the exchange.
"I want to find a mechanism to make more Filipinos be owners of shares. We'll definitely work on that," Yulo, who assumed the post on Monday, said in a television interview.
He was speaking after a week which has seen the sharpest falls in the market for more than two years on heavy selling by foreign investors.
He said the organisation and infrastructure of the exchange should be expanded beyond Manila.

"It is a question of bringing the stock exchange (to the restof the country)...and making it easier for Filipinos to participate...Once this is laid out properly, then I have a feeling that we will have an avalanche of Filipino investors buying stocks," he said.
Trading regulations, especially on insider trading, must be made clear and transparent to entice long-term investors and not just speculators into the market.
He said a massive education campaign on stock trading should be launched to achieve the goal.
"As I've said the task of making the stock exchange a national sport is a task that is for everyone ... It's everybody's ball game," Yulo said.
Yulo also said he remained confident that the Securities and Exchange Commission would give the bourse a self-regulatory status within this year.
The status was withheld after former PSE president Vitaliano Nanagas hastily resigned earlier in the year due to differences with staff and some brokers over his reforms.
